..
Issued at 309 PM EDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...Potential of Heavy Rainfall with Greatest Concern Saturday 
Night/early Sunday....

The primary forecast concern for this forecast will be potential of 
heavy rainfall, with greatest impacts possible Saturday night into 
Sunday AM.

Some elevated moisture return is approaching the IN/IL stateline 
this afternoon downstream of a stronger upper level short wave 
tracking across central Iowa. Some fairly dry mid level air 
preceding this zone of moisture advection should limit rainfall 
through late this afternoon with this initial elevated forcing. A 
more robust low level theta-e ridge will build in from northeast 
Illinois after 03Z this evening. Some question as to how strongly 
forced the setup will be late this evening, with potential of 
more widespread showers and embedded thunderstorms passably 
holding off until late overnight hours as upper jet streak 
noses into southern Great Lakes with deeper moisture profiles in
place. Some trimming of PoPs may be needed this evening across 
central/eastern portions of the area as initial mid level 
moisture advection forcing outruns better upper support. Did 
delay thunder mention a bit this evening with lapse rates 
looking meager as mid level moistening occurs, with greater 
thunder potential likely holding off until after 06Z.

Saturday through early Sunday afternoon still appears to be most 
potentially impactful period of this forecast with heavy rainfall 
potential the first order concern followed by some marginal severe 
threat south of US 24. Guidance has exhibited some dramatic shifts 
over past few days in the handling of mass fields with this system 
which appears to be in large part in difficulty handling the 
location and strength of the associated diabatic PV anomaly across 
the Mid MS Valley. Overall trend in 12Z guidance (although still 
with large variance) has been toward an initially weaker low/mid 
level diabatic PV anomaly and preference to more of a southward 
suppression of low level reflection into west central Indiana by 
midday Saturday. Some indications of a weak mid level dry slot 
feature punching into the area Saturday morning could provide a 
lull in greater shower coverage, but stronger upper support/DPVA
and northward migration of 500-1200 J/kg MLCAPE axis should 
allow for convective redevelopment in the afternoon. The 
downstream low level jet into east central Indiana may be a bit 
more subdued as a result of the initially more suppressed 
evolution tonight which could yield a bit lower of a severe 
threat from earlier indications Saturday afternoon. No 
significant changes noted in SPC Day 2 Outlook with Marginal 
Risk (mainly wind) across far southeast areas. Some locally 
heavy rainfall is possible Saturday afternoon with greatest 
potential across the south/southeast where greater instability 
should reside and where some enhanced low level convergence 
from low level jet could be situated.

The biggest potential impact with the system for this weekend is 
beginning to focus more on hydrology. PWAT's of 1.75 to 2.00 inches 
are expected to wrap around mid level height minimum into the local 
area Saturday into Saturday night. The track of the mid/upper height 
minimum across central Indiana and sharpening of low level trough 
axis should allow a deformation-forced region to form Saturday 
night into early Sunday AM. Very strong low level moisture 
convergence is possible from the combination of the weak 
southerly flow across the south and more robust easterly flow 
across the southern Great Lakes to maximize precip efficiency. 
Warm cloud depths are also expected to be in excess of 12k feet.
Some higher res guidance depicts an axes of very heavy rainfall
Saturday night an storm total rainfall amounts in excess of 5 
inches in area of strongest deformation forcing. Some 
consideration was given this afternoon to issuing a Flood Watch 
for Saturday night into Sunday AM. Upon collaboration, have 
opted to hold off on Flood Watch with this issuance given 
relatively dry antecedent conditions and very high run to run 
volatility in recent guidance with key low level mass features 
which will affect strength/position of deformation forcing.
Saturday night/Sunday AM does increasingly look like a period to
watch for hydro concerns however. 

Forecast confidence is below normal for early next week with 
guidance struggling in how to handle residuals of the mid/upper 
level system across Ohio Valley in weak steering flow/blocking 
pattern. Did accept blended guidance trend of maintaining PoPs into 
middle of the week but this will be subject to change given to low 
predictability of this pattern. A dampened upstream ridge by the 
middle of next week via a series of Pacific waves will allow 
potential of some renewed theta-e advection in wake of 
decaying/departing upper low with additional chances of storms 
Wed/Thu and trend back to seasonable temperatures.
